judged_text: TopicEmbed.import stores external content in posts with cook_method raw_html (line 22) and interpolates the feed-supplied url unescaped into the "<a href='#{url}'>" footer (line 13), so imported markup is rendered verbatim with none of Discourse's HTML sanitization — the Readability path's whitelist (lines 48-49) at most filters tag/attribute names and never URL schemes, so javascript:/data: hrefs survive, while the RSS path applies no content filter at all. Stored XSS on the Discourse origin: hostile RSS item bodies are stored as live script-bearing HTML, and a javascript: link planted on any embeddable-host page (e.g. a blog comment, which Readability keeps because a/href are whitelisted) executes attacker JS in the forum session of every user who opens the imported topic — session/token theft sitewide including staff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from external RSS bodies (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub`) or from Readability (`doc.content`). Neither path sanitizes HTML, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends a footer containing `#{url}` with only a prefix regex check (`/^https?\:\/\//`), so a malicious URL containing a single quote can inject attributes/markup. Together, this is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff.
